name.en: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) Account

authority: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, Government of India

description.en: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) is a national mission for financial inclusion to ensure access to financial services — a basic savings and deposit account, remittance, credit, insurance, and pension — in an affordable manner. Any Indian citizen above the age of 10 can open a zero-balance PMJDY account at any bank branch or Business Correspondent outlet.

verifiedConditions.claim: Any Indian citizen, including minors above 10 years of age, is eligible to open a PMJDY account. There is no minimum balance requirement.
PMJDY accounts are primarily for unbanked individuals. However, existing account holders can also open a PMJDY account to avail the scheme's benefits, subject to bank discretion.

unverifiedEligibility: Minors aged 10 and above can open accounts independently; below 10 requires a guardian.
Persons without any officially valid document can open a 'Small Account' with a self-certified photograph and signature/thumb impression, valid for 12 months.
One PMJDY account per household is eligible for the RuPay accident insurance cover and overdraft facility.

requirements.claim: Account opening form available at the bank branch or downloadable from the PMJDY portal. The form requires basic personal details, nomination, and consent for RuPay card issuance.
Any one Officially Valid Document (OVD): Aadhaar card, voter ID, driving license, PAN card, passport, or NREGA job card. If Aadhaar is available, no other document is required for KYC.

Address proof is required if the identity document does not contain the current address. Acceptable documents include utility bill, ration card, or a letter from the employer or any recognized public authority verifying the address.
Two recent passport-size photographs of the applicant.

processInformation.claim: Visit any bank branch or Banking Correspondent (BC) outlet. Nationalized banks, private banks, and regional rural banks all offer PMJDY accounts. The bank cannot refuse to open a PMJDY account for an eligible individual.

Fill the account opening form, attach the required documents, and submit at the bank counter. The bank will complete KYC verification using the submitted OVD. If Aadhaar is provided, e-KYC can be completed instantly.

The account is opened on the same day. A passbook is issued and a RuPay debit card is provided (may be dispatched by post if not available immediately). The account comes with a built-in accidental insurance cover of Rs. 2 lakh through the RuPay card.

processInformation.appliesTo: Account holders with satisfactory account operation
processInformation.claim: After six months of satisfactory operation, an overdraft facility of up to Rs. 10,000 is available (Rs. 5,000 without conditions for Aadhaar-linked accounts). Only one account per household is eligible for the overdraft facility.

output.claim: A zero-balance savings bank account with a passbook and RuPay debit card. The account includes an accidental death and disability insurance cover of Rs. 2 lakh, access to overdraft facility (after 6 months), and eligibility for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) from government schemes.

fees.claim: There is no charge for opening a PMJDY account. The account can be maintained with zero balance. There is no minimum balance requirement. The RuPay debit card is also issued free of cost.

processingTime.applicability: PMJDY account opening at bank branch
processingTime.claim: PMJDY account is opened on the same day of application at the bank branch if all documents are in order and KYC is completed. The RuPay debit card may take 7-15 days if dispatched by post.

sources.title: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana — Official Portal
sources.publisher: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The PMJDY portal provides comprehensive details on the scheme objectives, eligibility, benefits (zero balance account, RuPay card, accident insurance of Rs. 2 lakh, overdraft facility up to Rs. 10,000), and progress statistics.
claimsSupported: Zero balance savings account for every Indian citizen.
RuPay debit card with Rs. 2 lakh accidental insurance cover.
Overdraft facility up to Rs. 10,000 after 6 months of satisfactory operation.
sources.uncertainty: Overdraft and insurance benefits may be revised periodically. Individual bank branches may have varying turnaround times for card issuance.

sources.title: RBI Master Direction on KYC — Know Your Customer norms
sources.evidenceExcerpt: RBI KYC norms define Officially Valid Documents (OVDs) accepted for bank account opening: Aadhaar, voter ID, driving licence, PAN, passport, NREGA job card. Simplified KYC norms apply for small accounts.
claimsSupported: OVDs include Aadhaar, voter ID, driving licence, PAN, passport, NREGA job card.
Small accounts can be opened with self-certified photograph if no OVD is available.
e-KYC through Aadhaar enables instant account opening.
sources.uncertainty: KYC norms are updated periodically by RBI circulars. Digital KYC methods continue to evolve.

limitations: Overdraft facility availability depends on satisfactory account operation and is at the discretion of the bank.
Only one PMJDY account per person is permitted; duplicate accounts may be closed.
The Rs. 2 lakh accidental insurance cover through RuPay card requires at least one successful transaction in 90 days.
Small Account opened without OVDs has aggregate credit limits and is valid for only 12 months (extendable by 12 months if OVD application proof is submitted).
Interest rate on savings deposits is as per bank policy and may vary across banks.
State-specific implementation may vary in terms of BC network availability.

review.reviewReason: Core scheme benefits and eligibility are reviewed from the official portal. Bank-specific implementation and overdraft terms need periodic verification.
nextReviewTrigger: Changes to PMJDY scheme guidelines by Department of Financial Services.
Revision of RuPay insurance cover amount or terms.
Updates to RBI KYC norms affecting account opening requirements.
Changes to overdraft facility limits or eligibility criteria.
